refsect1.title: Unit specifications

note.para: These directories get cleaned up when vera starts. Garbled or misnamed unit specification files get removed. Overrides of units that no longer exist in @INSTALLCONFIGDIR@ also get removed.

refsect2.title: Filename requirements
refsect2.para: Names of unit specification files must follow these requirements. The valid characters in unit specification filenames are:

listitem.para: Lowercase letters a-z
Uppercase letters A-Z
Digits 0-9
A space, period, or a dash -
All characters with the high bit set, they are presumed to use the default system locale's encoding (but this is not checked)

refsect2.para: All other punctuations and characters are prohibited. Additionally:

listitem.para: A unit specification file's name cannot start or end with a space, period, or a dash
No two consecutive spaces, periods, or dashes
Maximum filename length is NAME_MAX-1 (254 octets)

refsect2.para: Files in the unit specification directories that do not meet these requirements get ignored (and removed during the next reboot).

note.para: vera reserves unit names prefixed by system/ for its internal use, specifically.

listitem.para: / implies that unit specification files can be installed in subdirectories, this is discussed in .
Enabling this unit results in it getting started automatically in the multi-user and graphical runlevels.

note.para: Hierarchical and compound units must use absolute dependencies, /system/multi-user and /system/graphical, for example. (see for more information).

listitem.para: Similarly, system/boot-required units get started in all runlevels, and before the runlevel-specific units.

refsect2.title: Format of unit specification files
refsect2.para: This section describes the format of unit specification files.

The validate command reads the filename and checks that it meets all formatting requirements. The command displays the parsed representation of the unit specification. validate also reads all existing unit configuration files from @INSTALLCONFIGDIR@ and prints a warning message if any dependencies in the filename do not exist. This is not an error. vera ignores non-existent dependencies to avoid unintentional typos.
validate assumes that filename gets installed in @INSTALLCONFIGDIR@. If it gets installed in a subdirectory it is necessary to spell out the full subdirectory path, as an optional parameter:
This is an example of validating the contents of the startup file that gets installed as @INSTALLCONFIGDIR@/web/startup.

note.para: Verifying the validity of dependencies requires that @INSTALLCONFIGDIR@ and its subdirectories are accessible to the userid that's running validate.

refsect2.para: The edit command provides a way to manually edit a unit specification file safely, with error checking. The edit command does the following:

listitem.para: The edit command makes a copy of any existing modified unit specification file that already exists in @LOCALCONFIGDIR@, otherwise the original unit specification file gets copied from @INSTALLCONFIGDIR@.
The copied file gets opened in an editor. The EDITOR environment variable specifies the editor (defaults to vi).

After the editor terminates (presumably after saving all changes to the edited file), the validate command checks the modified unit specification file. If all checks pass: the edited file gets installed in @LOCALCONFIGDIR@, then the edit command finishes.
Otherwise the edit command offers three options after showing all the error messages:
The edit command finishes without making any changes, the temporary copy of the unit specification file gets removed.
The editor runs again, this offers the option to fix the errors, then try to validate it again.

The edited unit specification file gets installed despite the reported errors. This option is available in case the errors come from other unit specification files and not the edited one's (the validate command checks all unit specification files that are currently installed).

refsect2.para: For completeness' sake, the revert command deletes the custom unit specification file for the named unit, from @LOCALCONFIGDIR@.
This is a slightly contrived example of a unit specification file that shows most of its possible settings:

informalexample.literallayout:
Name: scheduler Description: "System Scheduler"
Requires-First: - boot
Requires: - time_service - synchronization_service
Required-by: - calendar
Enabled: - system/multi-user - system/graphical
Starting: type: forking before: - conference_service - update_service after: - time_sync command: "/usr/bin/scheduler start"
Stopping: type: automatic after: - conference_service - update_service before: - time_sync command: "/usr/bin/scheduler stop"
Restart: "/usr/bin/scheduler restart" Reload: "/usr/bin/scheduler reload"
Version: 1

refsect2.para: Unit specification files use the YAML format. This documentation glosses over this detail, and describes the unit specification file format in more general terms.
However these are full YAML documents and can use any logically equivalent, alternative YAML syntax. For example:
This is a logically equivalent before setting from the previous example.
A unit specification file is a Key: value map. Keys are not case sensitive, name and Name are equivalent, and there are only two required keys:

listitem.para: name must be identical to the unit specification file's name.
version must be set to 1.

refsect2.para: A description is optional. version should be the last key in the file. Combined with all other requirements this allows direct installation of unit specification files, without any special procedures. No explicit action is required to notify vera to load them. Unit specification files get ignored unless they have a version: 1 and their name matches their filename. This means that:

listitem.para: When using package management software that installs packages by creating each file with a temporary name, then renaming the file after its contents are complete, vera ignores anything in @INSTALLCONFIGDIR@ that doesn't parse as valid YAML and without a matching name. In effect, it ignores the temporary files until they are renamed.

Even if a new unit specification file gets copied directly into @INSTALLCONFIGDIR@, as is: the unit specification file gets ignored without a version: 1. Placing this key at the end of a unit specification file results in them getting ignored until they are complete.

refsect2.para:
For these reasons there is no vlad command for installing updated vera unit specification files. This happens automatically, with
inotify 7 's assistance.

note.para: There's a brief delay before the updated unit specification files get reloaded. The default delay is controlled by the VERA_RELOAD_DELAY environment variable, and defaults to 6 seconds. Use the vlad setenv command to change the delay.

refsect2.title: Starting and Stopping
refsect2.para: The Starting key in a unit specification file contains other Key: value pairs that specify how this unit gets started.

listitem.para: This key gives the command that starts the unit's programs.
The starting type specifies how the unit gets started. The possible values for Type are:
The starting command forks and its child process is the permanent unit process. The original process terminates.
The starting process is the main unit process. After the starting process starts running the unit is considered to be fully started.
The starting process is the main unit process. After the starting process starts running the unit is considered to be fully started.
When the starting process terminates it gets immediately restarted.

note.para: respawn requires a starting command. For other starting types: an unspecified starting command has the same results as if the unit's starting command immediately terminated with an exit code of 0, for a forking unit. A oneshot unit without a starting command is effectively a placeholder. The unit is deemed to get started immediately, upon demand, with all the other implications that follow (other units' before and after dependencies, for example).

listitem.para: Timeout defaults to 60 seconds, if missing. A forking unit's starting command must terminate with a 0 exit code before this timeout expires.
Once the forking unit's starting command terminates with a 0 exit code the unit is deemed to be started (and other units that start after this get started themselves now).
In all other cases the unit's start is deemed to have failed (see below).
A timeout of 0 indicates an infinite timeout, there is no time limit for the starting command.
These keys specify other units that get started before or after this one (see ).

refsect2.para: The Stopping key in a unit specification file contains other key/value pairs that specify how this unit gets stopped.

listitem.para: This key gives the command that stops the unit's programs.
The stopping type specifies how the unit gets stopped. The possible values for Type are:
The unit gets stopped by running vlad stop for this unit, or if another unit that this unit requires gets stopped for any reason.
The unit also gets stopped when all of its processes stop. When the last process in this unit stops this has the same results as running vlad stop.
Only vlad stop stops this unit. The unit does not get stopped if other units required by it are stopped.

This is used by placeholder units that serve as runlevel targets, or as Required-By or Enabled dependencies, for example: many units are required by system/multi-user or other runlevels. If any of those units stop this does not stop the entire runlevel and all other units in it, even though system/multi-user formally requires them.

note.para: It's expected that the stopping command takes appropriate measures to terminate all processes that were previously started. In the event of an automatic stop there won't be any, but the stopping command is free to perform whatever bookkeeping a formal unit stop needs.

listitem.para: Timeout defaults to 60 seconds, if missing. A stopping command must terminate before its timeout expires.
A timeout of 0 indicates an infinite timeout, there is no time limit for the stopping command.
These keys specify other units that get stopped before or after this one (see ).

refsect2.para: After the stopping command times out or terminates any remaining processes in the unit (which may include a stuck stopping command) receive a SIGTERM signal, followed by SIGKILL.
Commands inherit the following environment variables:

note.para: RUNLEVEL and PREVRUNLEVEL are for init compatibility and contain the one digit init runlevel designations (or the full vera runlevel name for a non-default configuration that does not define init aliases).

refsect2.title: Starting failures
refsect2.para: An attempt to start a forking unit fails if its starting command times out or terminates with a non-zero exit code. This has the following implications:

listitem.para: Other units that require this unit but haven't started, and are waiting for the failed unit to start, do not get started any more.

The same actions that normally happen when the failed unit gets stopped also happen, as if the stop got executed for this unit, specifically: all other units that were started as a failed unit's dependency get now stopped.

refsect2.title: Reload and Restart commands
refsect2.para: The reload key and restart keys define the commands executed by vlad reload and vlad restart commands. These commands are allowed only if the unit is already started.

refsect2.title: respawn parameters
refsect2.para: A respawn starting type unit gets restarted up to three times in thirty seconds. This is to prevent a malfunctioning unit from slowing down the system. An optional respawn key adjusts these default settings:

informalexample.literallayout: Name: sshd Description: SSH server Starting: Command: /usr/sbin/sshd Type: respawn Respawn: attempts: 1 limit: 60

refsect2.para: Note that the type key in the starting section defines this unit as a respawning unit, and the standalone respawn key defines the respawning parameters:

listitem.para: This defines the maximum number of times the unit gets started before it gets limited.
This value in the number of seconds before the counter gets reset.

refsect2.para: vera starts this unit at most attempts times in limit seconds. If the unit fails one more time before limit seconds are up, vera waits until limit seconds expire, before attempting to restart the unit again.

note.para: This is only when the specified starting command exits normally with a 0 exit status. Any other exit status puts the unit into a penalty box until limit seconds expire before vera restarts the unit again.

refsect2.title: SIGTERM and SIGKILL
refsect2.para: A unit gets stopped by running its stopping command if its specified; then sending the SIGTERM signal to the remaining processes (subject to the settings below), giving them a few seconds to wrap things up on their own, and then immediately SIGKILLing any processes that remain.

informalexample.programlisting: Name: scheduler Description: "System Scheduler" Starting: type: forking command: "/usr/bin/scheduler start" Sigterm: notify: parents version: 1

refsect2.para: The Sigterm key in the unit specification file specifies how processes in the container receive a SIGTERM signal.

listitem.para: All processes in the unit's container get a SIGTERM.

Processes that are children of other processes in the same container and which run the same executable as their parent process do not receive a SIGTERM, only its parent process does. A child process that runs a different executable does get a SIGTERM normally.

refsect2.para: notify: parents is the default if the unit specification file does not have a stopping command. notify: all is the default if the unit specification file has an explicit stopping command, SIGTERM gets sent to all processes after the stopping command finishes.

refsect2.title: Alternative Groups
refsect2.para: An alternative-group names units which are not meant to be started at the same time. Starting an alternative-group unit automatically stops any other unit in the same alternative-group.

informalexample.literallayout:
Name: http-apache Description: Apache web server Alternative-Group: webservers
Version: 1 --- Name: http-nginx Description: Nginx web server Alternative-Group: webservers
Version: 1

refsect2.para: A unit in an alternative group should not have a Required-By dependency and other units should not have a Requireds dependency of an alternative group unit (see for more information).
Names of alternative groups are arbitrary labels that generally follow the same requirements as unit names (but are not unit names and exist in their own namespace):

listitem.para: They follow the same requirements as unit filenames and names (see for more information).

They are resolved according to their unit's hierarchy. If the above units are installed as networking/http-apache and networking/http-nginx then their alternative group's name is really networking/webservers (unless it's given as /webservers). See for a description of unit hierarchies.
